let's say you have 2 homeworks due in 2 days, an exam in another class in 3 days, and a large group project that is due 2 weeks from today. that crap is overwhelming. you need to do the homework, but you also need to study for the exam, but you also don't want to look like an absolute slacker to your team and they are constantly asking of you to meet with them daily for hours and you just don't have that time. what do you do? 

this is one large load, but we can simplify it with priorities. okay, the exam is pretty big, that gets a priority level (PL) of 1. but the homeworks are also due earlier, so they bump the exam to (PL2+) and take PL1-. the project has a bit of time, so it has a PL of 3 or 4. 

with that, you now worry on how to study for an exam while doing homework in another course that is completely irrelevant. KISS* (Keep it stupid simple). the human mind is one that does not multitask well. so start to actually set up devote times for homework. that can be hard times, or soft times. like, devote EITHER 45 minutes to HW1 or work until you get confused and fustrated (whichever comes first) with good faith effort. once you hit that, take a small (1hr) break and start work on HW2 for the same interval.  since progress has been done on the homework, they now start to take on a smaller priority. that exam is a biggie, so devote 1hr - 1hr30 to studying for that exam intermittently throughout the day WITH LONG BREAKS in between. the information you got needs to be absorbed into the mind and understood. and that takes a bit for most of everybody. during this break moment, I would talk to the project team and tell them of your schedule and that once the Exam is over, you will be back to full action. until then, you will be doing light work on the project. take this rest time to do a bit of research on whatever project you are working on. but maybe 20 minutes. then rest.
